A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLaCy research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; rotated appendix tables were also inspected.

before.justification: V3 reports original OU simulations, Rivers and AirQuality evaluations, and appendix experiments on sensitivity, nonlinear processes, negative controls, and acyclicity.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds experiments with multiple-testing correction and time-dependent mean reversion.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds optional false-discovery-rate adjustment of the resulting p-values. The sliding-window spectral fitting, extracted features, and Granger inference pipeline remain unchanged; the main experiments still omit this adjustment.

E1.justification: Appendix E.11 adds synthetic scenarios with sinusoidal and exponentially decaying mean-reversion coefficients, introducing explicitly time-varying process dynamics. The existing OU scenarios and both real-world datasets remain covered.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments, including the spectral baselines and Petersen controls. The additional checks reuse existing comparators: Granger and PCMCI for FDR correction, and Granger for time-dependent mean reversion.

E3.justification: Appendix E.8 introduces a corrected-testing protocol at N=5, C=0.5, sigma_b=0.5, and sigma_g=1.0. Appendix E.11 specifies new modulation settings, including gamma=1 and exponential decay rate 0.1. Existing experimental settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Adds targeted checks of whether the findings survive multiple-testing correction and whether endogenous spectral changes disrupt causal inference. Existing window/stride sensitivity, spectral PCMCI, nonlinear-process, negative-control, and acyclicity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V4 adds Benjamini–Hochberg correction and reports results under multiple-testing control. The stated 100-run averaging, 10 Rhino seeds, and existing uncertainty-reporting practice remain unchanged; no increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and appendix scores are unchanged. Tables 16–17 add FDR-corrected results, while Tables 19–20 add modulation results. For example, Table 19’s first row reports PLaCy versus Granger F1 of 0.49 versus 0.54, but TNR of 0.53 versus 0.47. These are new-condition findings.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 substantially revises the graph-preservation assumptions, explicitly requiring local stationarity, signal-dominated additive noise, spectral identifiability, and valid feature-space VAR inference. Theorem B.2 extends scaling to affine shifts and removes its predecessor’s independence-preservation claim. Theorem B.3 replaces an invalid modulus-distribution step with an approximation under explicit signal dominance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about spectral causal discovery, graph preservation, and empirical robustness. The revised formal qualifications do not change these headline statements.

C2.justification: Section 6 explicitly characterizes PLaCy as specialized for scale-free systems. Appendix E.8 recommends FDR correction for graph-level evaluation, and E.11 interprets the new experiments as evidence that endogenous spectral variation is not systematically mistaken for causal structure.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 explicitly documents discarding the zero-frequency component, without establishing a procedural change. Appendix E.11 supplies generation equations and modulation parameters. Table 11 hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, runtime information, and code/data access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Benjamini and Hochberg (1995) to support multiple-testing correction. The existing research positioning remains stable; bibliographic updates to works such as CausalGAN and CCM-Filtering concern the same cited research.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized copyedits, pluralizes the title, revises author/front-matter text, adopts author-year citations, and adds an Impact Statement. Some explanations are expanded, but most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into an ICML-style layout, changing typography, title block, headers, spacing, and display placement. Table 1 gains TNR summary rows, appendix table orientation is standardized, and four new result tables appear. All five existing figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: V4 replaces v3’s invalid spectral-magnitude proof step with an explicitly qualified approximation, clarifies theoretical boundaries, and adds useful multiple-testing and endogenous-dynamics checks. These improve mathematical transparency and validation. The gain remains bounded: the main empirical evidence is unchanged, and Appendix B still asserts preservation of linear independence despite the revised theorem proving only dependence preservation.
